From: Liam O'Hara <liam.ohara@aurorachain.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: detailed breakdown of subprocessor chain + egress paths for APAC pilot

Hi Vivek,

We're kicking off AuroraChain's APAC pilot next quarter and procurement asked for a single package that decomposes your subprocessor chain and the egress paths for any customer data originating in our APAC region. Specifically, they want: 1) an itemized list of all subprocessors (including second-tier subcontractors) that may process AuroraChain data; 2) a short description of role/responsibility for each (logs, metrics, model hosting, CDN, observability, etc.); 3) where data (including logs and metrics) may leave APAC and by which provider; and 4) confirmation of contractual controls (DPA clauses, SCCs or equivalent, KMS/HSM usage).

We attach our compliance intake template — if you can return a populated matrix and a one-page egress diagram that would speed approval. Timeline is tight: procurement has a cutover review on Aug 18 and would like artifacts by Aug 13.

Thanks,
Liam O'Hara
Head of Procurement
AuroraChain

Attachments: AuroraChain_DPA_Redline_v2.pdf, procurement_intake_template.xlsx

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask and the template.

Short answer: yes, we can produce the artifacts you need by the Aug 13 target. Next steps from our side: Naomi (legal/compliance) will provide the DPA amendment draft and a signed-by-default list of subprocessors; Kimberly (ops) will produce a concise APAC egress diagram and the matrix showing role/responsibility and data paths. I'll consolidate into a single ZIP and hand it to your procurement team.

Couple of clarifying requests to ensure we match your checklist:
- Do you need second-tier subcontractor contact info or just company names and country?
- For "where data leaves APAC" — do you want both transient control-plane routes (e.g., telemetry forwarded to a central observability cluster) and persistent storage egress?
- Any special encryption or residency attestations you need beyond SCCs + KMS usage?

Proposed timeline: we will send the subprocessor matrix (spreadsheet) and egress diagram by Tue Aug 11 EOD PT; the DPA amendment draft by Wed Aug 12. If that works, I will also open a DocuSign envelope for the DPA amendment (link will go to your legal contact).

I'll paste Naomi's and Kimberly's notes below once they weigh in.

Best,

Hi Liam / Vivek,

Thanks — quick note from legal/compliance. We will produce the following artifacts as separate files and also bundled:
1) Subprocessor decomposition matrix (columnar): subprocessor name; role (hosting, caching, CDN, monitoring, backups); country of processing; first-tier vs second-tier; contractual basis (DPA appendix / SCC / standard contractual clause).
2) Egress diagram (PDF/PNG): visual showing origin (APAC region endpoints), intermediate processors (edge CDN, logging aggregator), and final destinations (central US observability cluster, KMS region for key material).
3) DPA amendment draft (PDF): short amendment to enumerate processors and confirm our notification and objection process.
4) Evidence pointers: SOC 2 report dates (if available), KMS/HSM attestation summary, and our standard logging retention policy.

Controls and notes: all customer data in APAC is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.3 and at rest using per-customer keys (KMS). Observability telemetry is scrubbed for PII by default; where telemetry must contain identifiers (rare), we can provide a redaction plan or an isolated telemetry stream under a dedicated project. For any processors crossing borders we rely on SCCs and contractual safeguards; where required we can offer a limited residency-only config for the pilot (i.e., opt-out of forwarding to central analytics).

We will attach the draft DPA amendment and the populated matrix in our delivery. For procurement's convenience we will also produce a one-page "artifact index" that lists each file and the exact checklist item it satisfies.

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
